package_info.package_versions: Affected versions prior to Microsoft’s fix (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The ARM API for Azure API Management contained a vulnerability that allowed users with only Reader-level access to escalate their privileges by retrieving admin keys, enabling them to perform Contributor-level actions such as reading, modifying, and deleting APIM configurations. This bypassed intended access controls and exposed sensitive management operations to unauthorized users.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on-demand API call by Reader user)
execution_context.file_location: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API endpoint for APIM resource

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code issues a GET request to the ARM API endpoint for APIM, retrieving the admin keys for the APIM resource, which are then used to generate SharedAccessSignatures, granting full management access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reader-level users should not be able to retrieve admin keys or perform privileged management operations. This API call exposes sensitive credentials to unauthorized users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only Contributor or Owner roles should be able to access admin keys and perform management operations. Reader roles are expected to have read-only access without the ability to retrieve secrets or escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A Contributor or Owner legitimately retrieving admin keys for operational purposes.
key_indicators: API endpoint returning sensitive credentials to low-privilege users
Use of admin keys to generate SharedAccessSignatures for privilege escalation

execution_context.file_location: Direct Management API for APIM resource

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses the obtained admin keys to generate a SharedAccessSignature, which is then used to authenticate requests to the Direct Management API, allowing the attacker to perform any management operation (read, modify, delete) on the APIM resource.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of a SharedAccessSignature generated from admin keys obtained by a Reader-level user is a clear privilege escalation and abuse of access controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only authorized users with Contributor or higher privileges should be able to generate and use SharedAccessSignatures for management operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate admin automating APIM management tasks using valid credentials.
key_indicators: SharedAccessSignature generated from admin keys by a Reader
Direct Management API access from unexpected user roles
Unusual management operations following a Reader’s API call

attack_chain.action: Reader-level user calls the ARM API endpoint to retrieve admin keys for the APIM resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: Acquisition of admin keys, enabling privilege escalation.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the admin keys to generate a SharedAccessSignature.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as an admin to the Direct Management API.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the SharedAccessSignature to perform privileged management operations (read, modify, delete) on the APIM resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the APIM resource and potential access to further secrets and integrated systems.

behavioral_signatures: Reader-level users invoking ARM API endpoints that return admin keys
Generation of SharedAccessSignatures by non-privileged users
Direct Management API operations from accounts with only Reader permissions
file_indicators: No specific file indicators; detection relies on API call patterns and access logs
network_indicators: Unusual GET requests to /listKeys endpoints from Reader-level accounts
POST requests to Direct Management API endpoints using newly generated SharedAccessSignatures
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Azure activity logs for Reader-level accounts making calls to ARM API endpoints that return admin keys (e.g., /listKeys). Flag any generation or use of SharedAccessSignatures by users without Contributor or Owner roles. Correlate management operations on APIM resources with the privilege level of the initiating account, and alert on any management actions performed by accounts that should only have read access.
